name: spice-server
desc: Implements the server side of the SPICE protocol
why: Server side of the SPICE remote display protocol, a door into how remote desktop virtual machines stream graphics and input.

brief.what_it_is: SPICE server is the server-side component of the SPICE remote-access stack, which the SPICE project describes as a library rather than a standalone program. According to the homepage, the SPICE server is the library a hypervisor uses to share a virtual machine over the SPICE protocol. The homepage says the wider project covers remote viewing, audio, USB device sharing and folder sharing for VMs, and divides the stack into four parts: protocol, client, server and guest. The GitLab page describes this repository as the 'Server component.' Inputs and outputs are not spelled out in the pages I read; the homepage only says the client sends data and translates what comes from the VM so the user can interact with it.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says the project aims to provide a complete open source solution for remote access to virtual machines in a seamless way, so you can play videos, record audio, share USB devices and share folders without complications.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage splits SPICE into four components: the protocol, which is the specification for communication between the other three; the client, such as remote-viewer, which sends input and translates VM data for the user; the server, which is the library the hypervisor uses to share the VM; and the guest, which is software running inside the VM such as the QXL driver and SPICE VDAgent. The fetched pages do not describe the internal mechanism of the server library itself.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the Homebrew install was documented in the pages I read. The server is a library meant to be used by a hypervisor, so there is no first-run or configuration step visible here. For full functionality the guest side (QXL driver, SPICE VDAgent) must run inside the VM, per the homepage, but no install instructions for that were seen.
brief.standout: Unlike most remote-desktop tools, this is a library a hypervisor embeds rather than a server you run yourself, and the project frames the whole stack as four cooperating parts that include in-guest drivers. The Homebrew package is named spice-server and ships no executables.
brief.status: unknown. The GitLab repository page shows a 'Created on May 05, 2018' date and an LGPLv2.1 license, but it shows no last-release date or last-commit date, and the README body did not load. The homepage gives no release or activity information.
brief.caveats: The README body on GitLab did not load, so no build, usage or API details were available. The page also showed a GitLab admin notice about spam restrictions on new accounts, which concerns the forge rather than the project. The homepage was reachable. License per GitLab page: GNU LGPLv2.1. No platform limits were stated in the pages I read.
